claims: C1 the assistant is permitted to provide the office phone number of a public official
C2 the assistant should decline to respond to a request for that public official's personal phone number
C3 the ground for C2 is that a public official's personal phone number carries a high expectation of privacy
C4 the same public official's office number and personal number fall on opposite sides of this clause

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule that carries root authority, the level the rules in the privacy-protection section of the document are given

concepts.name: privacy_context_dependence
concepts.gloss: whether information I counts as private or sensitive is not settled by I alone but depends in part on the context in which it is sought or used

concepts.name: public_official
concepts.gloss: P is a person holding public office, so that part of P's contact information exists to be reachable by the public in that role

concepts.name: office_phone_number
concepts.gloss: the first argument N is a phone number that reaches the second argument P in P's official capacity - a number attached to the office P holds rather than to P as a private person

concepts.name: personal_phone_number
concepts.gloss: the first argument N is the second argument P's own private phone number, held by P as a private person and not published as a way of reaching the office P holds

concepts.name: requests_number
concepts.gloss: the first argument Q is a request in the conversation asking the assistant for the second argument N, a particular phone number
concepts.inference: the span speaks of requests for a particular number, so a relation between a request and the number it asks for must exist for the rule to range over

concepts.name: high_privacy_expectation
concepts.gloss: N is information about a person that the person may expect to be kept private, because it belongs to their private life rather than to a public role they occupy

ontology.gloss: N is information about a person that the person may expect to be kept private, because it belongs to their private life rather than to a public role they occupy

asserts.read_back: the assistant may provide %, because it is the office phone number of public official %
the assistant should decline to respond to request %, because it asks for %, which carries a high expectation of privacy
the assistant is not to provide %, the personal phone number of public official %
asserts.inference: declining to respond to a request for the personal number is incompatible with supplying it, so the obligation to decline carries a prohibition on the act it declines

closure.reason: the span settles only two poles - a public official's office number, which may be given, and their personal number, which may not - and says nothing about any other number, so it does not settle what silence about those means
the span treats declining as the correct response where a high expectation of privacy is at stake and nowhere bars declining, so silence about declining leaves it permitted
